agent_notes: Reviewed addition of shutdown_drain_timeout to settings page/save flow. The new field follows the existing safe_int/safe_float pattern: form input is parsed via safe_float(form.get(...), 60.0, 1.0, 3600.0) in triggarr/web/validation.py, which explicitly rejects non-finite values (math.isfinite guard) and clamps to [1.0, 3600.0] before the result is re-validated by the pydantic SettingsModel (shutdown_drain_timeout: float = Field(default=60.0, ge=1.0, allow_inf_nan=False) in triggarr/models/config.py). Settings are written via the existing atomic TOML write path with os.chmod 0o600, inside the existing search_lock. Field construction into new_config uses an explicit allowlist (no **form unpacking), so no mass-assignment risk. No injection, XSS, secret-exposure, or auth-bypass vector was found in the diff; this is a tightening/validation addition consistent with established conventions, not a weakening of any control.

The diff matches 75-02-PLAN Task 1 (D-02/D-03) exactly. The GET context key and the POST safe_float parse follow the established per-field pattern used by the safe_int fields next to it (tracking_window_minutes, max_consecutive_failures). There is no pattern deviation.

The import change only extends the existing triggarr.web.validation import with safe_float. It adds no new module dependency and no cycle. triggarr/search/scheduler.py already imports triggarr.web.routes lazily, inside a function (update_info, _sync_auth_state, lines 544/550). That predates this diff and is unaffected.

The scheduler does not consume the new config field yet. Neither _read_shutdown_drain_timeout (scheduler.py:58-75) nor the module constant _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT (scheduler.py:81) reads settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout, and the drain path at lines 611-656 still uses the import-time constant. Until 75-03 (wave 2: local resolution at shutdown, config default with env override) lands, the UI value is saved but has no effect. This is expected given the phase's wave split, but 75-02 and 75-03 should merge together before any release so the UI knob is not a no-op.

The default and floor are written twice: once on the GeneralConfig Field (default=60.0, ge=1.0) and once at the safe_float call site (60.0, 1.0). Every existing safe_int call site already repeats its config default this way, so this follows the established convention and is not flagged. If the Field default changes, the form fallback can drift from it.

The UI ceiling of 3600.0 is deliberately tighter than the config model, which has no upper bound (CONTEXT D-01: 'the form-parse clamp (D-03) supplies a practical UI ceiling'). Side effect: a value above 3600 set by hand in TOML is clamped to 3600 on the next settings save. If the 75-02 Task 2 input carries max=3600, browser validation could instead block form submission entirely while the rendered value exceeds 3600. Worth one test or a conscious decision when Task 2 lands.

findings.title: Every settings save silently resets shutdown_drain_timeout to 60.0 because the form never submits the field
findings.why_it_matters: Any unrelated settings save silently erases a drain timeout that was set in config.toml. After the scheduler starts honoring the config value, this means shutdowns cut off too early or the timeout no longer matches stop_grace_period.

findings.fix_hint: Either add le=3600.0 to the model field or document that config values above 3600 are clamped by the UI.
findings.problem: GeneralConfig.shutdown_drain_timeout has no upper bound (models/config.py:139, ge=1.0 only). The form clamp caps the value at 3600.0, so a value above 3600 set in config.toml is lowered to 3600 the next time the form round-trips it. The config comment at models/config.py:138 says this ceiling is intentional ('form clamp (3600.0) is the UI ceiling'). This is a tightening, so it is reported under the cap. pending: confirm whether values above 1 hour are meant to be supported in config.toml. If they are, the model and the form bound should agree.
